configuration: Nine of the thirteen upstream cases of unittest/liegroups.cpp over the sixteen joint models and the eight Lie group types, every operand read from ic/<ic>/operands.json rather than drawn from lg.random(), randomConfiguration or Eigen's ::Random. Upstream runs each case 20 times and the per-joint sweep 51 times per pass; this check runs each once.
observable: the Lie group operations of the configuration manifold: integrate, difference, interpolate, distance and normalize on every joint group, and their Jacobians, the parallel transport along an integrate step and the tangent map on each of the eight Lie group types the manifold is composed from
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that the operands are frozen rather than drawn and every repeated sweep runs once instead of 20 or 51 times
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero component of every frozen item in ic/nominal/operands.json. Perturbing every component rather than one was measured, not assumed: with a single component per item, 18 of cpp-explog's 48 observables and 6 of cpp-spatial's 76 came back with a spread of exactly zero, because a relative change of 2.2e-16 in one entry of a rotation matrix rounds away in the last bit of an output built from all nine. Every component still moves by exactly two units in the last place, so this stays the generic two-ulp noise calibration rather than a physics experiment. A component that is exactly zero is never perturbed, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is a meaningless perturbation of a physical quantity and a parser hazard besides. The worst measured spread is 4.2188e-15 absolute. One item is deliberately exempt: the two quaternions of small_distance_test, whose graded observable IS the distance between them, about 3e-17. Moving each by two units in the last place is a change of the same size as the quantity itself and collapses the distance to zero, which breaks upstream's own assertion that it stays strictly positive. Measured, not assumed. 83 of the 426 observables show a spread of exactly zero and are insensitive by construction, not by accident. They are quantities that are constant for the group they belong to: the neutral configuration, and, on the vector-space and planar-rotation groups and at zero velocity on every group, the derivatives of integrate and difference and the tangent map, all of which are then the identity matrix or its negative. One more is the small-distance case, whose two configurations the variant deliberately leaves untouched, for the reason given above. Their bound therefore rests on the physical argument in the warrant rather than on a measured sensitivity, and a reviewer should read it that way.
altbuild: none: the same official.cpp compiled at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off against the same pinned source reproduces the -O2 result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. Eigen fixes the evaluation order of these expressions and the arithmetic is scalar, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead. The probe was repeated on the worker on 2026-09-14 (x86_64, inside the env image); the result was unchanged, bit-identical.

warrant: The graded quantities are the Lie group operations of the configuration manifold: integrate, difference, interpolate, distance and normalize on every joint group, and their Jacobians, the parallel transport along an integrate step and the tangent map on each of the eight Lie group types the manifold is composed from, in SI units and in the coordinate order the joint model, the Lie group or the spatial type fixes, which is part of the input and not something an implementation chooses. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 2.60e+00, it admits about 1.03e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this test can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a transposed motion subspace, a rotation composed in the wrong order, a dropped Taylor branch near the identity, a sign error in a cross product or a missing scaling on a mimic joint each move individual values by between 1e-2 and 1e+2 in these units, seven to eleven decades above the bound, and a relative error of one part in a thousand injected into the largest graded value of this check lands 2,536,492 times over it. Every upstream identity also stays active, so such a fault is rejected twice over. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these expressions differs by about n eps |x|, roughly 30 * 2.2e-16 * 2.60e+00, which is decades inside the bound. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst of the 3,468 graded values by 4.2188e-15, using 4.173e-06 of the bound, that is 239,633 times of headroom, and the alternative build measured exactly zero. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
